sentence: We will show that if you start with any n numbers on the board (with n ≥ 2) and in every move you choose two numbers and replace each of them by their sum, then it is possible to eventually “equalize” all numbers (i.e. arrive at a situation where all n numbers are equal) by a suitable choice of moves if and only if n is a power of 2.

sentence: The answer to the problem is: It is possible to obtain n identical numbers by a finite sequence of moves if and only if n is a power of 2 (that is, n = 2ᵐ for some positive integer m).
sentence-category-reason: States the final result explicitly as an if and only if statement.

sentence: For the game described – where in each step you select two numbers and replace both by their sum – it is possible to obtain a situation where all n numbers become equal if and only if n is a power of 2.
sentence-category-reason: Restates the final result succinctly.

sentence: Thus, if someone asks “For which n (n ∈ ℤ⁺, n ≥ 2) can the n numbers be made identical in finitely many steps?

sentence: ” the answer is: exactly those n of the form n = 2ᵐ (with m a positive integer).
